steps.title: What the scheduler does every tick

content.value:
Each tick, the CommandScheduler loops through every active command.

For each one it calls execute().

If a command's isFinished() returns true, the scheduler calls end() and removes the command.

This is the heartbeat of command-based.

Every command has four phases:

initialize() runs once when scheduled.

execute() runs every tick.

isFinished() tells the scheduler when the command is done.

end() runs once for cleanup.

The scheduler automatically walks each command through this lifecycle.

In initialize(), use schedule() with an InstantCommand that calls telemetry.addData() with any key and value, then calls telemetry.update(). InstantCommand runs its lambda once and finishes immediately.

Add a second schedule() call with another InstantCommand.

The scheduler runs both — the first finishes instantly, then the second.

Every command-based OpMode follows this pattern: you schedule commands, the scheduler runs them.
